entities.evidence: This Enoch fathers Methuselah, identifying him as Jared’s son in Genesis 5:18.
Methuselah is named as the son whom Enoch fathered at age sixty-five.

analysis.evidence: חֲנוֹךְ (Enoch) is the subject of וַיְחִי. The phrase חָמֵשׁ וְשִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה gives the duration, sixty-five years, and וַיּוֹלֶד introduces the next event, when Enoch fathered Methuselah.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix
analysis.sense: to live for a stated length of time

analysis.evidence: חֲנוֹךְ is the subject of וַיְחִי and וַיּוֹלֶד. The verse says that Enoch was sixty-five when he fathered Methuselah, identifying him as the son of Jared in this genealogy.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In חָמֵשׁ וְשִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה, חָמֵשׁ supplies the five in “five and sixty years,” Enoch’s age when he fathered Methuselah.

In חָמֵשׁ וְשִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה, וְ joins five and sixty to give Enoch’s age of sixty-five years when he fathered Methuselah. The Haqor article for שֵׁשׁ explicitly assigns both “six” and “sixty” the root key שדש. Its ד represents a historical consonant preserved in Sabaic s¹dṯy “sixty”.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed conjunction וְ (“and”) + cardinal numeral שִׁשִּׁים, common gender, plural absolute.

analysis.evidence: In חָמֵשׁ וְשִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה, the singular שָׁנָה supplies the unit for sixty-five. With וַיְחִי חֲנוֹךְ, the phrase gives Enoch’s age when he fathered Methuselah.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Enoch is the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד, and אֶת marks Methuselah as its direct object. The verse records that Enoch fathered Methuselah at age sixty-five.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed conjunction וַ־

analysis.evidence: In וַיּוֹלֶד אֶת מְתוּשָׁלַח, “he fathered Methuselah,” אֶת marks the personal name מְתוּשָׁלַח as the direct object of וַיּוֹלֶד.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Enoch (חֲנוֹךְ) is the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד ‘he fathered’, and אֶת marks מְתוּשָׁלַח as its direct object, identifying Methuselah as his son. The verse-final form has pausal שָׁ in place of dictionary-form שֶׁ.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name in pausal form, without prefix or suffix.
